title: $Lf^*$ preserves bounded constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of the
setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$ is bounded constructible
([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is $Lf^*K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$
([sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]).

proof.text: First verify exactness for every commutative condensed ring, not just the admissible adic rings. On abelian sheaves the tensor product is closed symmetric monoidal and tensoring preserves colimits, hence is additive and right exact [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Thus the module categories in question are abelian [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian]. The inverse image $f^*_{\Ab}$ is exact [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact]. The functor $\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})$ commutes with the forgetful functors by [def-sfb-modobj-transport]; apply [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted] to conclude it is additive and exact. By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso], $\alpha_f$ is invertible for this arbitrary $\Lambda$. Extension along it is naturally isomorphic to $\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f^{-1}}$ [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso]. Restriction is the identity on underlying objects and morphisms [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], so the same lifted-exactness lemma, now with underlying functor the identity of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, proves this restriction exact. Consequently the composite $f^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})$ of [def-sfb-module-upper-star] is additive and exact. This argument applies to every morphism of schemes, including the maps between strata and covers used below.

source.place: First sentence: exactness of the module-object pullback; expand its two factors

proof.text:
Represent $K$ by a complex $C$ and take a K-flat resolution $P\to C$. By the definition of the total derived composite [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], $Lf^*K$ is represented by $f^*P$. The exact-functor cohomology isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], applied to the exact functor of step 1, gives
$$H^q(Lf^*K)=H^q(f^*P)\simeq f^*H^q(P)\simeq f^*H^q(K).$$
The last isomorphism is induced by the quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$. Choose a finite interval $[a,b]$ outside which $H^q(K)=0$, as in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. An additive functor sends the zero object to a zero object, so the displayed formula gives $H^q(Lf^*K)=0$ outside the same interval. It remains to check constructibility of $f^*M$ for any constructible module $M$.

source.place: First two sentences: termwise computation, cohomology, and boundedness

proof.text: For any scheme map $h:V\to U$, transport sends the regular $\Lambda_U$-module to the regular $h^*_{\Ab}\Lambda_U$-module: both actions are the transported multiplication, by [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. Set $R=h^*_{\Ab}\Lambda_U$ and $S=\Lambda_V$. In [def-sfb-modobj-extension], $S$ is an $S$-$R$-bimodule with right action $\mu_S(\operatorname{id}\otimes\alpha_h)$. Apply [lem-sfb-mixed-bimodule-right-unitor] to this mixed bimodule. Together with [def-sfb-module-upper-star] it gives $e_h:h^*\Lambda_U\simeq\Lambda_V$, induced by multiplication. Its two inverse maps and linearity are supplied by the cited statement. Additivity from step 1 sends finite biproducts of this regular module to the same finite biproducts, including the empty biproduct.

source.place: Last sentence: the regular-module comparison, extracted from inherited step 6

proof.text: We use exactly the general ring-object constructibility in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. By [def-sfb-constructible-module] and [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented], a constructible $M$ has a finite stratification $i_a:Y_a\hookrightarrow Y$ and pro-étale covers $u_{ai}:U_{ai}\to Y_a$ on which its transported restrictions have finite presentations [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. These initially use the coefficient ring $u_{ai}^*{}_{\Ab}i_a^*{}_{\Ab}\Lambda_Y$. Relabel along its canonical isomorphism to $\Lambda_{U_{ai}}$, obtained from [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. This relabelling is extension of scalars and is exact by the argument of step 1 (extension along an isomorphism is inverse restriction). It sends the regular module to the regular module by the mixed-bimodule right unit, just as in step 3 with the sheaf functor the identity. Thus it sends a cokernel of a map between finite sums of the former ring to such a cokernel for $\Lambda_{U_{ai}}$. The definition [def-sfb-module-upper-star] identifies the relabelled module with $u_{ai}^*i_a^*M$. Hence choose finite presentations $u_{ai}^*i_a^*M\simeq\operatorname{coker}(A_{ai}:\Lambda_{U_{ai}}^{m_{ai}}\to\Lambda_{U_{ai}}^{n_{ai}})$. The entries of $A_{ai}$ may be arbitrary sections; no scalar-constant presentation has been assumed.

source.place: Choose stratification and cover: distinguish general local finite presentations from scalar-constant presentations

proof.text: Put $X_a=X\times_Y Y_a$, with maps $j_a:X_a\to X$ and $f_a:X_a\to Y_a$. By [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification] these maps give a finite stratification of $X$ with images $f^{-1}(|Y_a|)$. The schemes $X,Y$ are of finite type over the field $k$ by [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Their topological spaces are Noetherian, and their locally closed strata are constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Thus this is a stratification of the kind required by [def-sfb-constructible-module]. Empty strata may be removed; no reduced scheme structure or equality of scheme-theoretic fibres with set-theoretic preimages is assumed.

source.place: Stratification and its inverse image; retain constructibility of the strata

proof.text: For each $a$, form $V_{ai}=X_a\times_{Y_a}U_{ai}$, with projections $v_{ai}:V_{ai}\to X_a$ and $h_{ai}:V_{ai}\to U_{ai}$. The arrows $u_{ai}$ are weakly étale and the family is fpqc, by the covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. Base change preserves weak étaleness [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change] and preserves fpqc covering families [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. Hence $(v_{ai})_i$ is again a pro-étale cover of $X_a$. These results impose no Noetherian, finite-type, surjectivity-of-each-arrow, or quasi-compactness-of-each-arrow assumption, so they apply to the chosen cover.

Pullback composition [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] gives the required comparison on this cover. Indeed $f j_a=i_a f_a$ and $f_a v_{ai}=u_{ai}h_{ai}$, and therefore
$$v_{ai}^*j_a^*f^*M\simeq v_{ai}^*f_a^*i_a^*M\simeq h_{ai}^*u_{ai}^*i_a^*M.$$
Thus it suffices to pull back the finite presentation of $u_{ai}^*i_a^*M$ along $h_{ai}$. This uses composition of module-object pullbacks, rather than an underived base-change assertion about pushforwards.

source.place: The restriction identity obtained by composition of pullbacks

proof.text:
Apply $h_{ai}^*$ to the chosen presentation of step 4. Exactness from step 1 preserves its cokernel and the regular-module comparison of step 3 identifies the finite free terms. Consequently
$$h_{ai}^*(u_{ai}^*i_a^*M)\simeq\operatorname{coker}(h_{ai}^*A_{ai}:\Lambda_{V_{ai}}^{m_{ai}}\to\Lambda_{V_{ai}}^{n_{ai}}).$$
By [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module] this is finitely presented, with the same finite ranks, which may be zero. Step 7 identifies it with $v_{ai}^*j_a^*f^*M$. Relabelling back along the inverse canonical coefficient isomorphisms preserves finite presentations by the argument in step 4. The cover in step 6 therefore witnesses local finite presentation of $\operatorname{mapMod}(j_a^*{}_{\Ab})(f^*M)$ over $j_a^*{}_{\Ab}\Lambda_X$, precisely [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented].

source.place: Last two sentences: right exactness applied to a finite presentation

proof.text: Steps 4–8 give a finite constructible stratification on which the transported restrictions of $f^*M$ are locally finitely presented. Thus $f^*M$ is constructible in the sense of [def-sfb-constructible-module]. Apply this to $M=H^q(K)$ for each $q$. The isomorphisms of step 2 show that every $H^q(Lf^*K)$ is constructible, and step 2 supplies the same finite cohomological interval as for $K$. These are exactly the conditions of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Therefore $Lf^*K$ is bounded constructible.

source.place: Conclusion: boundedness and constructibility of cohomology
